q.description: Search query for Bing Maps (e.g., 'coffee', 'restaurants', 'hotels near Times Square'). Use specific location queries for better results.

cp.description: GPS coordinates formatted as 'latitude~longitude' (e.g., '40.7455096~-74.0083012'). Specifies the center point for the search area.

count.description: Number of results per page (maximum 30). Controls how many results are returned.

first.description: Result offset for pagination (defaults to 0). Used to retrieve subsequent pages of results.

setlang.description: 2-character ISO 3166-1 language code for localization (e.g., 'us', 'de', 'gb'). Sets the language for results.

no_cache.description: Set to true to bypass cached results and force a fresh API call.

place_id.description: Unique reference identifier for a specific location. Can be used independently of the q parameter to retrieve details about a specific place.

q.description: Search query for DuckDuckGo Maps (e.g., 'Coffee', 'Italian restaurants', 'Hotels').

lat.description: GPS latitude coordinate for the search center point. Must be used together with lon parameter. Cannot be used together with bbox parameter.

lon.description: GPS longitude coordinate for the search center point. Must be used together with lat parameter. Cannot be used together with bbox parameter.

bbox.description: Bounding box coordinates formatted as 'latitude_tl,longitude_tl,latitude_br,longitude_br' where tl=top-left and br=bottom-right. Cannot be used together with lat/lon parameters. Use this to constrain search results to a specific geographic area.

strict_bbox.description: Controls strict bounding box adherence. Set to 1 (default/strict) to limit results strictly within the bbox, or 0 (off) to allow results outside the bbox boundaries. Only relevant when bbox parameter is used.

query.description: Search term or phrase for the DuckDuckGo search.

examples: Live music in Austin this weekend
query.description: Search query for events, specifying the topic, type, or name.

start.description: Only 0 is supported. Google Search does not paginate event listings with this offset.

query.description: The financial search query. This can be a company name, stock ticker symbol (e.g., 'AAPL', 'GOOG'), or a broader financial topic (e.g., 'US stock market trends', 'latest fintech news'). Prefer exchange-prefixed ticker symbols (e.g., 'NASDAQ:AAPL') over company names alone — name-only queries may return empty or generic results, and common names can match multiple entities, leading to misattributed data.

no_cache.description: Force SerpAPI to fetch fresh results instead of returning cached data. Set to true to bypass cache and get the most up-to-date information.

profile_id.description: Facebook Profile ID or username to retrieve information for. Can be a numeric ID (e.g., '100080376596424') or a username (e.g., 'Meta'). This is the unique identifier for the Facebook profile or page.

q.description: Optional search query to refine results. Works with 'all', 'visual_matches', or 'products' types.

hl.description: Two-letter language code for localized results (e.g., 'en', 'es', 'fr', 'de').

url.description: The URL of an image to perform Google Lens visual search. Must be a publicly accessible image URL.

type.description: Search type to filter results. Options: 'all' (default), 'products' (shopping results), 'exact_matches' (identical images), 'visual_matches' (similar images).

country.description: Two-letter country code for localized results (e.g., 'us', 'uk', 'ca').

q.description: Search query for Google Maps (e.g., 'coffee shops', 'restaurants near Central Park').

ll.description: GPS coordinates for the search, formatted as '@latitude,longitude,zoom_level'. Required when using pagination (start parameter). If unspecified and start is not provided, search may be less geographically specific or use a default location. Results are strictly viewport-bound to the area defined by the coordinates and zoom level; adjust coordinates and paginate via `start` to cover adjacent areas.

start.description: Starting result index for pagination, used to get subsequent pages of results. When start is provided, ll parameter becomes required. For the first page, omit start (or use start=0 only if ll is also provided).

hl.description: Two-letter language code for the interface language (e.g., 'en' for English, 'es' for Spanish).

num.description: Number of results per page. Maximum 100, defaults to 20.

sort.description: Sort articles by 'title' or 'pubdate'. Default is by citation count.

start.description: Result offset for pagination. Defaults to 0.

view_op.description: View specific sections. Use 'view_citation' to view a specific citation or 'list_colleagues' to list colleagues.

no_cache.description: Force fresh results, ignoring cached data. Set to true to bypass cache.

author_id.description: Unique identifier of the author from Google Scholar. Required to fetch the author's profile.

citation_id.description: Required when view_op='view_citation'. Unique identifier for the specific citation to view.

q.description: The ID of an individual Google Scholar organic search result. This is required to fetch citation information for a specific paper.

hl.description: Two-letter language code for localization (e.g., 'en' for English, 'es' for Spanish, 'fr' for French).

no_cache.description: Force fresh results, ignoring cached data. Set to true to bypass cache (cache expires after 1 hour).

num.description: Number of image results to return. Defaults to 20 if not specified. Google typically returns up to 100 results.

query.description: Query to find images; be specific about the topic or subject. Avoid single-word or vague queries; combine subject, style, context, and audience details for precise results.

num.description: Maximum number of results to return per page. Default is 10, maximum is 100.

query.description: Search query for finding relevant news articles. Overly long or overly specific queries may return empty results; simplify to key phrases and split multi-concept searches into separate queries.

start.description: Result offset for pagination. Use 0 for the first page (default), 10 for the second page, 20 for the third, etc.

num.description: Maximum number of results to return per page. Default is 10, maximum is 20.

query.description: The search query for Google Scholar. This can be an academic topic, paper title, author name, or specific keywords.

start.description: Result offset for pagination. Use 0 for the first page (default), 10 for the second page, 20 for the third, etc.

examples: what is the capital of France?
query.description: User's search query; should be a clear, concise question or keyword phrase.

q.description: Search query for Google Images. Supports Google search operators like inurl:, site:, intitle:.

gl.description: Two-letter country code to define the country for the search.

hl.description: Two-letter language code to define the language for the search interface.

imgar.description: Aspect ratio filter. Options: s (square), t (tall), w (wide), xw (extra wide).

imgsz.description: Image size filter. Options: l (large), m (medium), i (icon), etc.

start.description: Result offset for pagination. Must be between 0 and 999.

device.description: Device type for the search. Options: desktop (default), tablet, mobile.

engine.description: Set parameter to google_images_light to use the Google Images Light API engine.

end_date.description: End date for filtering images by upload date. Format: YYYYMMDD.

location.description: Geographic location for the search origin. Specify at city level for best results.

start_date.description: Start date for filtering images by upload date. Format: YYYYMMDD.

image_color.description: Color filter for images. Options: bw (black and white), red, blue, green, yellow, orange, pink, white, gray, black, teal, brown.

period_unit.description: Time period unit for filtering by upload date. Options: s (second), n (minute), h (hour), d (day), w (week), m (month), y (year). Must be used with period_value.

period_value.description: Time period value to use with period_unit. Specifies how many units back to search.

google_domain.description: Google domain to use for the search. Defaults to google.com.

attrs.description: Attribute filters to refine search (e.g., 'HotAndNew' for new businesses, 'Deals' for businesses with offers). Can be comma-separated for multiple filters.

start.description: Result offset for pagination. Use to fetch additional results beyond the first page. Each page typically contains 10 results.

sortby.description: Sort order for results. 'recommended' shows Yelp's recommended matches, 'rating' shows highest-rated first, 'review_count' shows most-reviewed first.

find_loc.description: Location to search in (e.g., 'San Francisco, CA', 'New York, NY', '10001'). Can be a city, state, address, or ZIP code.

no_cache.description: Set to true to force fresh results from Yelp, bypassing SerpApi's cache. Useful when you need real-time data.

find_desc.description: Search query describing what to find (e.g., 'pizza', 'coffee shop', 'italian restaurant'). This is the business type or service you're looking for.

yelp_domain.description: Yelp domain to search on (e.g., 'yelp.com' for US, 'yelp.ca' for Canada, 'yelp.co.uk' for UK). Defaults to yelp.com if not specified.

num.description: Maximum number of results to return per page. Default is 10, maximum is 100.

query.description: Product or item to search for on Google Shopping.

start.description: Result offset for pagination. Use 0 for the first page (default), 10 for the second page, 20 for the third, etc.

query.description: Search query/queries for Google Trends (use comma for multiple). Format (single vs. multiple terms) is dictated by `data_type`.

data_type.description:
Specifies Google Trends search type, dictating `query` format (single term or comma-separated multiple terms).
Options:
- `TIMESERIES`: Interest over time; single/multiple queries.
- `GEO_MAP`: Regional comparison; multiple queries.
- `GEO_MAP_0`: Regional interest; single query.
- `RELATED_TOPICS`: Related topics; single query.
- `RELATED_QUERIES`: Related queries; single query.
